# findPerson — POST /people/find

Find a person matching the given criteria

## Verified behaviors

- **A name alone returns 404 Unmatched even when the person exists** — A 404 Unmatched does not mean the person is absent. Criteria that fall short of the minimum combination are never matched at all, and the answer is indistinguishable from a genuine no-match. ([replay](../behaviors/find-below-threshold-is-unmatched.md))
- **A vanId in the body wins over every other criterion** — When the body carries a vanId, the rest of the criteria are not used to search — they are not even checked for agreement. A name that belongs to nobody still matches, so a caller who sends a stale vanId alongside fresh details gets the stale record back. ([replay](../behaviors/find-by-vanid-overrides-criteria.md))
- **Following the 302 returns the whole person, not the match stub** — A client that follows the redirect never sees the `{vanId, status}` stub — it ends up on GET /people/{vanId} and receives the full record with 200. This only works if the client converts to GET, as fetch and browsers do; `curl -X POST -L` keeps the method and gets 411. ([replay](../behaviors/find-followed-redirect-returns-the-person.md))
- **Only certain criteria combinations are matched at all** — The endpoint does not attempt a match until the criteria reach one of a fixed set of combinations. Below that it answers 404 Unmatched rather than 400, so an under-specified query is silently indistinguishable from a person who is not there. ([replay](../behaviors/find-minimum-match-combinations.md))
- **With duplicates, name-based criteria return the first-created record** — When several records match, exactly one vanId comes back and nothing in the response says the match was ambiguous. Criteria including a name resolve to the oldest record. ([replay](../behaviors/find-returns-first-created-duplicate.md))

## Behavior

Attempts to match a person in the database. Read-only: never creates person records (use POST /people/findOrCreate for that).

Outcomes:

- **The body supplies a `vanId` that exists** — that person is returned as a **302** and every other criterion is ignored, no threshold involved.
- **One person record matches** — **302 Found**, with a `Location` header pointing at `/people/{vanId}` and a small match-stub body, `{"vanId": …, "status": "Matched"}`.
- **Several person records match** — still a **302** for exactly one of them, and nothing in the response says the match was ambiguous. Which one you get depends on the shape of the criteria; see **When more than one person record matches** below.
- **Nothing matches** — **404** with `{"vanId": null, "status": "Unmatched"}` (a match stub, not the standard error envelope).
- **The criteria fall short of the minimum combination** — **404 Unmatched** as well, not a 400, and indistinguishable from a genuine no-match. This is the common case to guard against; see **The criteria must reach a minimum combination** below.

## The criteria must reach a minimum combination

This endpoint is deliberately conservative — it would rather return nothing than return the wrong person. It does not attempt a match at all until the criteria reach one of these combinations:

- first name + last name + **email address**
- first name + last name + **phone**
- first name + last name + **zip5** + **date of birth**
- first name + last name + **street number + street name + zip5**
- **email address** on its own (a **phone** on its own matches too, though the docs list only email)

Anything short of that — a name on its own, name + date of birth, name + zip — comes back **404 Unmatched** regardless of who is in the database.

**A 404 here does not mean the person does not exist.** It usually means you did not supply enough to identify them. Do not treat Unmatched as "not in the database", and in particular do not follow it with a create — see POST /people/findOrCreate, which silently creates a duplicate for exactly this reason.

**If all you have is a name, use GET /people instead.** That endpoint is a loose prefix search with no threshold: `GET /people?firstName=Harriet&lastName=Kowalski` returns full person records for every candidate, and you decide which one (if any) is your person by inspecting them. Use /people/find only once you hold a strong identifier.

## How the criteria are compared

- Everything you send must agree with the person record. Adding a **wrong** first name to a correct email turns a match into Unmatched — extra criteria narrow, they never widen.
- Comparison is case- and format-insensitive: `HARRIET.KOWALSKI@EXAMPLE.COM` matches the stored lowercase address, `907-555-4242` matches the stored `9075554242`, and per the docs it is accent-insensitive too ("Pérez" matches "Perez"). Names may match on nicknames and variants unless the context has "Disable Partial Matching" turned on.
- The address combination needs the street **number**: `742 Evergreen Terrace` + zip matched; `Evergreen Terrace` + the same zip did not. A wrong zip with a right street also fails.

## When more than one person record matches

Duplicates are common in VAN databases, and this endpoint does not warn you about them: **it returns exactly one vanId with no indication that others also matched.** A 302 is not proof that the match was unique.

The pick is deterministic, but the tiebreak depends on the shape of the criteria — with three identical person records (102719047 < 102719048 < 102720144, same name, email and phone):

- criteria **including a name** (name+email, name+phone, name+dob+zip) → always the **lowest vanId**, i.e. the oldest person record
- criteria **without a name** (email alone, phone alone) → always the **highest vanId**, i.e. the newest person record

It is not the best-matching person record and not the most recently updated one: enriching the newer duplicate so it matched the criteria at least as fully did not move a name-based match off the oldest person record, and touching either duplicate changed nothing.

The consequence to plan for: at the threshold you may be handed a stale or partial duplicate, and a follow-up write through POST /people/{vanId} then lands on whichever duplicate won the tiebreak while the other keeps drifting. When it matters that you have *the* person record rather than *a* person record, list the candidates with GET /people and reconcile them yourself.

## Differs from the official docs

- **the operation** — Official docs imply a 200 with a person object on match. Sandbox probing (2026-08-03) shows 302 + Location on match and 404 with a match stub on no match; no 400 was observed even for sparse criteria like firstName-only. Criteria below the documented minimum combinations are also answered 404 Unmatched rather than rejected, so under-specified requests are indistinguishable from genuine no-matches. The docs are also silent on ambiguous matches: when several person records satisfy the criteria the API returns one of them with no indication that others matched.

## Example

```bash
curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/find' \
  -u "app-name:$NGP_API_KEY|1" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
  "firstName": "Harriet",
  "lastName": "Kowalski"
}'
```

See [PersonMatchCriteria](../schemas/PersonMatchCriteria.md).

## Responses

| Status | Meaning | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | Never sent by this endpoint. This is where a redirect-following client *lands* on a match: ``` POST /people/find {"firstName": "Ada", "lastName": "Testperson", …} ← 302 Found Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/102714507 {"vanId": 102714507, "status": "Matched"} GET /people/102714507 ← client re-issues the request at Location ← 200 OK { full person record — the body documented here } ``` requests, httpx, fetch and `curl -L` all follow that redirect and downgrade POST to GET by default, so a match reaches your code as this 200 and a full `Person`, never as the 302 and its two-field match stub. The no-match 404 is not a redirect, so the practical test is `resp.status_code == 200` vs `404`, not `302` vs `404`. The follow-up GET has no `$expand`, so its related collections come back null — re-fetch through the `getMatchedPerson` link if you need addresses, phones or emails. Gotcha: `curl -X POST -L` keeps the method across the redirect and re-POSTs to `/people/{vanId}` — the *update* endpoint — where IIS answers `411 Length Required` because the re-issued request carries no body. Drop the explicit `-X POST` (`-d` already implies POST) and curl downgrades to GET like everything else. | [Person](../schemas/Person.md) |
| `302` | A person matched the criteria. `Location` header points at the canonical person resource. | `PersonMatched` |
| `400` | Validation error, as the standard JSON envelope. ([details](../ERRORS.md#badrequest)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `401` | Missing/invalid API key, or a database mode the key does not have access to. ([details](../ERRORS.md#unauthorized)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `404` | No person matched the criteria. This is also the answer when the criteria never reached the minimum combination needed to attempt a match at all — there is no 400 and nothing in the body distinguishes the two cases. **Read it as "not identified", not "not in the database":** a person you can see through GET /people will still come back Unmatched here if all you sent was their name. See the operation description for the combinations that do trigger a match. | `PersonUnmatched` |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded. ([details](../ERRORS.md#toomanyrequests)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) |
| `500` | Internal server error. ([details](../ERRORS.md#servererror)) | [ErrorResponse](../ERRORS.md#errorresponse) or [AspNetError](../ERRORS.md#aspneterror) |

### `302` body — PersonMatched

An existing person was found and nothing was written. The only match-stub shape that accompanies a 302: from find, findOrCreate, create when the body's vanId exists, and update.

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vanId` * | integer |  |
| `status` * | any |  |

`*` = required.

### `404` body — PersonUnmatched

No person matched and nothing was written — the 404 body from find.

| Property | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vanId` * | null |  |
| `status` * | any |  |

`*` = required.
